decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up approach to the red nut on the left and gray nut on the right, lifting and turning downward gradually.
Finish vertical approach above the red and gray nuts, keeping separated elbow-up arms; refine alignment from wrist views before grasping.
Fine-center nuts in wrist views, lower to grasp height, close fully, then lift slightly to check retention.
Both nuts appear retained. Lift clear and carry each above its same-color bolt, then inspect coaxial alignment.
Correct fore-aft alignment of the carried nuts and descend cautiously toward the bolt tips, monitoring offset and contact.
Lower both retained nuts toward thread engagement with small lateral centering corrections. Check tip-to-hole alignment before tightening.
Attempt a slow clockwise tightening stroke on both aligned nuts, with minimal downward feed and closed grippers.
Release and unwind the wrists without turning the nuts backward; inspect whether both nuts remain seated on their bolts.
Red remains on its bolt; re-center and tighten another stroke. Gray has tipped off alignment, so withdraw the right gripper for a recovery view.
Continue tightening red while moving the right gripper above the tipped gray nut for a careful recovery grasp.
Release the seated red pair and lift clear. Approach the upright blue nut with the right hand; defer the sideways gray nut until the remaining upright pair is handled.
Lower the right gripper around the blue nut while parking the left arm clear of the central transfer area.
Fine-center the blue nut, close the right gripper fully, and lift to verify retention before transferring it centrally.
Carry the retained blue nut into the central staging area, keeping the left arm parked and maintaining clearance.
Set the blue nut upright at the workspace boundary and release it for a sequential left-hand pickup.
Withdraw the right hand from the staged nut first, then begin the left-hand approach while keeping the arms separated.
Approach the staged blue nut with the left hand and inspect a top-down recovery grasp of the tipped gray nut on the right.
Grasp and lift the centrally staged blue nut with the left hand. Withdraw the right hand; the gray bolt and nut require a clearer recovery view.
Correct the rejected tensor; no previous motion occurred. Carry blue above its bolt and approach the upright gray nut.
Center and lower blue toward its bolt. Regrasp the upright gray nut, then lift it clear for renewed alignment.
Refine blue's tip-to-hole alignment. The gray grasp was empty, so reopen and approach the nut again using its updated visible position.
Seat blue more centrally and start a clockwise stroke. Raise and reorient the right gripper to avoid its finger contacting the nearby gray bolt.
Blue has not seated; correct its lateral offset without further tightening. Grasp gray with the reoriented fingers and lift to check retention.
Lift blue slightly to clear contact and correct toward its visible bolt tip. Gray is retained; carry it above its bolt for a fresh alignment.
Descend slowly toward both bolt tips with small image-based lateral corrections; defer rotation until insertion is visible.
Begin a gentle clockwise stroke on blue now that its tip enters the hole; lower gray toward engagement without rotating it yet.
Pause tightening: neither bolt is centered reliably. Relieve contact slightly and make small lateral corrections using the rotated wrist views.
Use the visible bolt tips to refine coaxial alignment and lower both nuts a few millimeters, without twisting against misalignment.
Make millimeter-scale centering corrections so the bolt tips fill the nut openings before another tightening stroke.
Reset the open left wrist while the centered blue nut settles. Apply a slow clockwise tightening stroke to gray with very little feed.
Blue fell beside its bolt; reposition for recovery. Correct gray using head-view geometry and remove wrist tilt before trying further engagement.
Regrasp blue using the wrist-view offset. Lift gray clear of the bolt to inspect its retained orientation rather than forcing misaligned contact.
Reopen and lower for a deeper blue grasp while removing wrist tilt. Straighten gray and make a small head-view alignment correction above its bolt.
Close on the centered blue nut and lift it toward the bolt. Shift gray gently toward its visible bolt tip while lowering only a few millimeters.
Refine both retained nuts toward their bolt tips; gray is closer to coaxial alignment, so use only millimeter corrections there.
Gray now appears nearly coaxial; apply a slow tightening stroke with minimal feed. Lower blue slightly to engage its visible tip.
Relieve contact and correct lateral alignment rather than continuing to twist; use both head and wrist views to reassess the bolt centers.
Try a short seated blue tightening stroke. Lift gray farther clear and restore a vertical wrist axis before another alignment attempt.
Lift blue off contact and make a measured lateral correction. Shift gray toward the visible bolt axis while maintaining clearance.
Use the measured image response to center both bolt tips horizontally, then descend without rotation for a fresh engagement check.
Test a small fore-aft alignment correction at fixed height; compare the visible bolt-tip position before further insertion.
Continue the confirmed centering direction by three millimeters, then test a short clockwise stroke with negligible feed.
Align the bolt axes horizontally in the rotated wrist views, keeping height nearly fixed and avoiding additional twisting until centered.
The blue axis is now centered; refine gray by two millimeters, seat both gently, and test a short clockwise turn within wrist limits.
Release both nuts and unwind the wrists for another tightening stroke, checking that the nuts remain upright on their bolts.
Neither nut stayed seated. Lift clear, reset to a consistent vertical grasp orientation, and approach their new upright table positions.
Descend vertically onto both upright nuts with reduced jaw spread to avoid the adjacent bolts, keeping a consistent grasp orientation.
Close around the centered nuts and lift straight up, checking retention before repositioning over the bolt axes.
Bring retained blue over its bolt using the visible axis. Retry gray with a deeper grasp and reduced opening to avoid the adjacent bolt.
Lift blue for an unobstructed axis check. Move the right gripper toward the gray nut's fore-aft center before closing and testing its lift.
Use head-view projection to correct blue toward the bolt's base axis before lowering. Lift gray further to distinguish retention from table contact.
Blue's head-view axis now agrees with the bolt base; descend vertically without lateral drift. Retry gray at a deeper grasp height with moderate jaw opening.
Compensate blue's off-center grasp by turning around the nut rather than the wrist origin. Recenter gray fore-aft, close, and lift to verify a centered grasp.
Correct blue's remaining lateral offset with contact relieved. Reposition gray fore-aft while high, then descend vertically so the fingers do not push it.
Turn blue gently about its estimated nut center with minimal feed. Lift and reorient the right fingers to avoid the adjacent bolt before retrying gray.
Continue blue's compensated tightening arc with a tiny centering correction. Center and level the right gripper before descending around gray.
Release blue and reset the wrist to test whether it remains seated. Center the gray nut between the fingers, close fully, and lift.
Blue did not stay seated; approach its updated table position for a centered grasp. Move the retained gray nut above the bolt's head-estimated base axis.
Grasp blue centrally and lift. Bring gray down toward its bolt while correcting the visible horizontal offset in the wrist view.
Retry blue with a deeper, centered grasp. Lift gray off obstructed contact and shift toward the bolt before checking alignment again.
Relieve the blue grasp contact, level and recenter the fingers. Lower gray vertically from clearance to inspect actual tip engagement.
Make a smaller image-based blue centering correction, close, and test lift. Refine gray laterally by millimeters while seating gently without twisting.
Carry the centered blue grasp above its bolt. Lift gray out of obstructed contact and shift toward the visible bolt axis before another insertion.
Lower the centered blue nut vertically toward the tip. Make a small gray lateral correction and remove residual wrist tilt while holding its height.
Seat both nuts farther with slow vertical motion, correcting blue's small horizontal offset; inspect contact before rotating.
Turn blue slowly at fixed height, compensating its small grasp offset. Test a millimeter-scale fore-aft correction on gray before lowering further.
Continue blue's slow compensated tightening stroke within the wrist limit. Move gray along the confirmed centering direction while keeping its height fixed.
Correct blue's remaining tip offset without further wrist rotation. Lower gray a few millimeters now that the visible cap is entering the opening.
Make a final small blue centering correction, release, and reset its wrist. Turn gray about the estimated nut center to compensate its off-center grasp.
Withdraw from the unsuccessful seating attempts. Reset the left gripper above blue for a centered pickup, and lift gray clear for restaging.
Descend onto blue using its wrist-view center. Carry gray away from the bolt to a clear restaging location for a centered regrasp.
Center and lift blue with a straight grasp. Set gray down away from its bolt and release it for a better-centered pickup.
Move the centered blue grasp above its bolt. Descend vertically around the restaged gray nut without lateral contact.
Refine blue's alignment while descending toward insertion. Close on the restaged gray nut and lift straight up to verify the improved grasp.
Seat blue with a fore-aft centering correction, pausing before rotation. Carry the improved gray grasp above its matching bolt with clearance.
Refine the fore-aft axes using the bolt shaft and base rather than only overlapping hole pixels; keep blue's height fixed and lower gray cautiously.
